name: Comfortable Rib Breathing
cues: Find a supported sitting or lying position.
Breathe gently, allowing the lower ribs to widen.
Let the ribs settle naturally as you breathe out.
Keep shoulders relaxed; do not force or hold the breath.
readiness: Choose a comfortable position within your care team's recovery advice. This is an optional breathing practice.
adjustment: Use pillows or sit more upright. Return to normal breathing if uncomfortable or lightheaded.

name: Pelvic Floor Release
cues: Rest in a comfortable supported position.
Breathe slowly and allow the pelvic floor to soften as you inhale.
Allow a natural return as you breathe out.
Do not squeeze, push down or strain.
readiness: Use only while comfortable. Persistent pelvic pain or difficulty relaxing needs individual pelvic health advice.
adjustment: Keep the breath easy. If trying to release creates tension or discomfort, stop and ask your clinician.

name: Gentle Ankle Movement
cues: Sit or recline with your legs comfortably supported.
Slowly point your toes away, then bring them toward you.
Add small ankle circles each way if comfortable.
Move gently without forcing your range.
readiness: Follow your maternity team's movement advice, particularly after surgery or complications.
adjustment: Use smaller movements. Stop if uncomfortable, and ask your maternity team about any movement restrictions.

name: Short Easy Walk
cues: Choose a level route with a nearby place to rest.
Walk at an easy, comfortable pace.
Finish before pain or fatigue builds; a short outing is enough.
readiness: Begin when ready and within your maternity team's advice. Ask about readiness after caesarean birth or complications.
adjustment: Shorten the route or rest. Add activity gradually only as recovery allows; stop if painful.

name: Gentle Pelvic Floor Lift and Release
cues: Only practise if this exercise is appropriate in your individual care plan.
Gently close and lift around the back and front passages, breathing normally.
Fully relax before repeating; never bear down.
Do not practise by interrupting urine flow.
readiness: Wait until any urinary catheter is removed. Ask for individual advice if painful or hard to release.
adjustment: Follow your clinician's own hold and repetition advice. Stop if symptoms increase or full relaxation is difficult.

name: Side-Lying Core Connection
cues: Only try this if recommended for your recovery.
Lie comfortably on your side with knees slightly bent.
Inhale gently; as you exhale, softly draw in the lower tummy, then release.
Keep breathing. Stop for pain, pressure, leakage or tummy doming.
readiness: Ask your clinician or pelvic health physiotherapist about technique and suitability, especially with symptoms or an abdominal separation.
adjustment: Use a smaller effort and pillows for comfort. Do not strain or push through symptoms; seek individual advice.
